seo.title: Session Replay - Watch Real User Sessions | OpenPanel
seo.description: Session replay in OpenPanel: watch any user session next to its events, with text and inputs masked by default. Open source, 30-day retention, no replay quota.

hero.heading: See exactly what your users did
hero.subheading: Replay any user session to see clicks, scrolls, and interactions. Privacy controls built in. Loaded async so it never slows down your site.

related_features.title: Session tracking
related_features.description: Structured session data—entry pages, event timelines, duration—without requiring replay.

related_features.title: Event tracking
related_features.description: Custom events appear alongside replays in the session timeline.

related_features.title: Funnels
related_features.description: Jump from a funnel drop-off step directly to the session replay to understand why.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about session replay with OpenPanel.

items.question: Is session replay enabled by default?
items.answer: No. Set sessionReplay: { enabled: true } in the web SDK config. Nothing is recorded until you do, and only the web SDK records; there is no replay for React Native.

items.question: Does enabling session replay slow down my site?
items.answer: No. The recorder is not part of the main SDK bundle. It loads after your page is interactive, records in the background and sends chunks every 10 seconds, at most 200 events or 1 MB per chunk, and flushes when the tab is hidden. Use sampleRate to record a share of visits instead of all of them.

items.question: How is this different from Hotjar or FullStory?
items.answer: Three things. Recording is masked by default, so text and inputs never leave the browser unless you unmask a selector. The replay sits on the session page next to the events you already track, so you can jump from a funnel drop-off to the recording. And OpenPanel is open source: self-host it and the recordings stay in your own ClickHouse. OpenPanel does not have heatmaps, rage-click detection or console logs; if you need those, Hotjar or FullStory still make sense.

items.question: Are form inputs recorded?
items.answer: No. All inputs are masked by default (maskAllInputs), and so is all text (maskAllText). Hidden inputs such as CSRF tokens are always blocked. You can unmask specific text with unmaskTextSelector, and block whole elements with the data-openpanel-replay-block attribute.

items.question: How long are replays stored?
items.answer: 30 days from the start of the session, on Cloud and on self-hosted installs. The storage table has a 30-day TTL; there is no setting to keep them longer.

items.question: Can I block specific parts of my UI from being recorded?
items.answer: Yes. Add data-openpanel-replay-block to any element and it becomes a grey box in the recording. You can also pass your own blockSelector or blockClass in the config.

items.question: Does session replay work with self-hosted OpenPanel?
items.answer: Yes. Recordings go through the same ingest and land in your own ClickHouse, compressed, with the same 30-day TTL. The web SDK loads the replay script from your own instance.
